common_name: Apollo Alstroemeria (Classic White Peruvian Lily with Yellow Throat)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Apollo is a long-established white-flowered cut-flower cultivar.

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, handling the brittle roots carefully. Apollo bears clean white flowers with a yellow-flecked throat and fine maroon speckling on the upper petals, a classic, long-established cultivar prized in the cut-flower trade for its clear color and excellent vase life. It blooms over a long season from late spring into fall, and pulling rather than cutting spent flower stems from the base stimulates continued rebloom by removing the seed-forming stem entirely. In colder zones mulch heavily for winter protection or lift the roots for storage, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring if flowering declines.

common_name: Friendship Alstroemeria (Classic Salmon-Pink Cut-Flower Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; a long-established salmon-pink cultivar widely grown in the commercial cut-flower trade.

directions: Plant tuberous roots about six inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, handling the brittle roots carefully. Friendship bears warm salmon-pink flowers with a yellow-flecked throat and fine darker speckling on the upper petals, a soft, blended color that has kept it a long-standing favorite in the cut-flower trade for its excellent vase life and reliable production. It blooms over a long season from late spring into fall, and pulling rather than cutting spent flower stems from the base stimulates continued rebloom by removing the seed-forming stem entirely. In colder zones mulch heavily for winter protection or lift the roots for storage, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring if flowering declines.
